routing_warnings.description: The instructions to use Global Dough without the word Truck and retain the strapline belong to the logo text-content Requirement.
The request for fresh original ideas belongs to the original-artwork Requirement.
The requests for versions with and without the black box and for colour variants belong to the final-logo-variants Requirement.
The request for file types usable across online, print, truck, menu, banner, and uniform applications belongs to the usable-file-package Requirement.
The explanation that the logo lettering is custom-made and the offer to recommend complementary fonts primarily supports the brand-font-guidance Requirement.
The detailed requests concerning the flame O, typography size, strapline contrast, and letterform character modify the visual design rather than the revision-process obligation.
The selected option and request for additional typographic character change the logo's visual design.
The requested U, H, and D letterform changes are visual-design modifications; the request itself is not an implementation Event for the revision-process Requirement.
The reported PNG opening and display problems concern file usability rather than which visual variants must be included.
The freelancer's executed check of PNG opening and transparency display concerns the usable file package rather than the required visual variants.
The inaccessible colour-codes document is evidence for the Brand Colour Specification Requirement rather than the logo file package.
The request for a matching or complementary font belongs to the Brand Font Guidance Requirement.
The client's preference for the colours shown in the draft concerns the logo's visual design, not delivery of usable colour-code documentation.
The colour-codes document error concerns the independently defined brand-colour specification Requirement.
The AI, EPS, PSD, and PNG accessibility issues concern the usable logo-file package rather than font guidance.
The requested changes concern letterform appearance, word sizing, and strapline contrast rather than the logo's textual content.
The feedback changes typography character and colour treatment without changing the required business name or strapline.
The requested U, H, and D letterform adjustments concern visual styling rather than textual content.
Delivery of initial drafts supports the concepts and revision process but does not establish that the artwork is original.
The client selects the final visual version but does not verify that the artwork is original or non-AI-generated.
